title: Valid local model path not detected, missing config.json, and what to put in Original model source
body: A local path means the PC running the TurboForge service. Click Select folder / Select GGUF file to fill the path, or paste it manually; paired quotes and leading/trailing spaces from Windows copy-as-path are supported, and spaces inside the directory are preserved. A path existing does not mean the model files are complete or the conversion route is supported. Put a complete original HF checkpoint in "Model" and leave its "Original model source" empty; for GGUF pick the specific file. Supported self-contained files generate their resources automatically; other routes need a matching config.json and tokenizer.json/tokenizer.model, which can come from a separate local original HF directory or an explicit original repository. Do not treat a folder containing only GGUF as the original source again; GGUF import does not require original Safetensors when only metadata is needed. A single-file Qwen3.5 dense Q8_0 GGUF with hidden_size=1024 and complete embedded metadata can generate config.json, tokenizer, and chat template directly, without an original directory; other files of unknown origin must not have their config guessed from the file name. When there is no matching import route, use the original full-precision model as the input model and re-inspect instead of pretending support by adding only config.json; unsupported hardware or models must stop explicitly.
aliases: what to fill in original model source
no upload does not mean no input

title: A clean machine with only one GGUF: where does the original model directory come from
body: The release bundle contains no models, but a supported single-file GGUF does not need the developer's local original model directory. A complete Qwen3.5 dense Q8_0 GGUF with hidden_size=1024 can generate frontend resources in the gguf-resources cache from its embedded structure parameters, vocabulary, BPE merges, special tokens, and chat template, and convert with the GGUF as the only weight source. After selecting the GGUF, leave Original model source empty; this route is also recognized when an older version mistakenly filled the GGUF's own directory and it has no config.json. The recipe qwen3_5_gguf_standalone decodes and re-encodes to Q8_0, which is not byte-for-byte lossless, so quality must be verified separately; the current adapted engine caps context at 1024, applied automatically after the guided check. Files with missing fields, duplicate tokens, or unverified MTP stop explicitly — no guessed config and no silently dropped heads. Other architectures/precisions/shards are outside the current standalone import validation. The first run still prepares dependencies and the adapted engine; the generated resources, conversion, GPU load, and text generation of this 0.8B Q8_0 have been measured, but a full deployment on a clean PC has not.

does adding config.json make it work

title: HF automatic quality gate and independent evaluation corpus
body: In guided mode, new HF quantization enables the quality gate by default; no evaluation file needs to be provided. The default is WikiText-2 test at pinned revision b08601e04326c79dfdd32d625aee71d232d685c3, up to 2048 tokens; calibration uses train, and hashes and scores are recorded. The reference is the CPU FP32 PPL of this run's post-processing, pre-quantization weights, which costs extra RAM/time. NInfer still needs a matching baseline artifact and corpus; a packed import cannot prove its own quality. General English PPL does not guarantee results on every task.

title: Can it start without a network, and what does offline use need
body: The first start needs the internet to install missing Python/web dependencies; conversion also downloads uncached models, environments, and calibration/evaluation sets. Once fully prepared, local models and offline help work. Remote AI Q&A still needs a connection to the configured service; a clean PC cannot be promised to work offline out of the box.

title: Qwen3.5 AWQ support and why it is disabled
body: GPTQModel 7.10.0: New Qwen3.5 AWQ quantization did not pass local quality acceptance and is disabled; choose GPTQ or NInfer. Existing AWQ files support only verified native import; quantization is never redone automatically. Disabled model_type: qwen3_5, qwen3_5_text. Other architectures cannot claim measured quality on this basis either.

title: GPTQ/AWQ default inference backend and environment dependencies
body: The current default backend is AUTO; GPTQModel picks an available kernel for the current device and layout, and it is not guaranteed to be faster for every model. Torch is the explicit compatibility option. Dependency versions: GPTQModel 7.10.0, {'transformers': '5.20.2', 'datasets': '5.2.0', 'safetensors': '0.8.0', 'torchao': '0.18.0', 'pypcre': '0.6.4'}; Windows acceleration dependencies: {'triton-windows': '3.8.0.post29', 'flash-linear-attention': '0.6.0', 'fla-core': '0.6.0', 'einops': '0.8.2'}. The script prepares an isolated environment automatically, with a PyPcre wheel for the supported Python version, so no manual C++ compiler install is needed.

title: I know nothing about models — what do I do first?
body: Double-click the launcher → pick a local model/public HF link → inspect → choose the recommendation → automatic preparation and conversion → check validation → start; explain the single necessary input for each step now

title: Must I install Python, Node, or CUDA?
body: The bundle and source development differ; the one-click script prepares Python/page/dependencies as needed, and a built bundle needs no Node; the driver must work, and no arbitrary environment is guaranteed to auto-repair

title: Are AMD, Mac, or CPU-only supported?
body: The current one-click target is Windows x64 + supported NVIDIA; a CPU conversion option exists but has no speed measurement for this model, and it does not mean all GPU inference can switch to CPU

title: How long online and how much download?
body: First-time dependencies/models can be large; later runs reuse the verified cache; explain stages from the task log — never estimate completion minutes from the model name

title: I already installed these dependencies — why download again?
body: Check the actual worker/dedicated environment and versions; system Python is not the task environment; HF and NInfer environments are separate

title: The window closes after double-click and the page will not open?
body: Read the startup failure text and `.turboforge/logs/`, run `Start TurboForge.bat --check`; troubleshoot unbuilt page, permissions, network, and port separately

title: 8090 will not open — is it broken?
body: One-click start may pick another free port; use the actual URL shown in the startup window; the model API port defaults to the port of the first origin in the .env allowlist (template 18080) and is a different service

title: Do I need administrator rights or a driver upgrade?
body: Read the specific error first; never elevate by default. When the driver is unsupported, follow the official driver requirements — the script does not modify drivers automatically

title: Can I close the command-line window?
body: The current startup window hosts the page service; closing it interrupts tasks and the owned model process may be released with it; distinguish refreshing the page from closing the service

title: Can I use it without configuring AI?
body: Yes; model conversion and the help center are independent; AI is an explanation entry, not a runtime prerequisite

title: What goes in the local model path, and why is an existing path still invalid?
body: The path belongs to the PC running the TurboForge service; select or paste it, paired quotes and leading/trailing spaces are supported, and spaces inside the directory are preserved. For a complete HF fill the model directory and leave Original model source empty; for GGUF pick the specific file. Path exists, files complete, and route supported are three independent checks — handle the explicit missing item

title: Which kind of Hugging Face link do I enter?
body: Use a model repository or an explicit file/revision link; with multiple GGUFs pick the specific file and keep the explicit version; not an arbitrary web page link

title: Why does a private or gated model fail to download?
body: Verify legitimate repository access and license; never ask the user to send an access token to the assistant, and never promise to bypass restrictions

title: Can a clean environment with only one GGUF convert?
body: The release bundle contains no models and cannot depend on the developer's existing directories. First check whether it is a supported standalone import; for other routes verify the original repository — a declaration is parsed automatically, otherwise the user provides the original repository link to fetch only config/tokenizer. A complete Qwen3.5-0.8B Q8_0 single file is supported to generate resources from embedded parameters/vocabulary/merges/template and import standalone, with no original directory; it decodes and re-encodes to Q8_0, is not lossless, and caps context at 1024; missing metadata or other unsupported layouts still must not guess config

title: Why does a GGUF still need the original model, and what if config.json is missing?
body: The supported self-contained Qwen3.5-0.8B Q8_0 GGUF generates config/tokenizer/template automatically; leave Original model source empty. For other routes the original model source should be a matching HF directory with config.json and tokenizer.json/tokenizer.model, or the original repository; a directory containing only GGUF does not qualify. GGUF import does not require original Safetensors when only metadata is read; NVFP4 may need original full-precision tensors. Supplying files still must pass architecture/size support checks — config must not be forged

title: What are shards, and can I continue with one missing?
body: Multiple files together form the complete checkpoint; a missing shard stops the run — supply it from the original repository; never forge tensors

title: The file name says NVFP4 — why was it not recognized?
body: Real evidence is required: quantization config, packed weights, scale/block layout; the name alone is not enough

title: Same model name — why can others convert it but I cannot?
body: Check revision, architecture/geometry, actual format, source completeness, and engine version. The small-model NInfer route needs an adapted bundle; the developer's local adaptation must not be treated as a capability of the plain official engine everywhere; an unknown environment cannot be promised as accepted

title: Can an existing `.ninfer` change bits again?
body: It is not a general `.ninfer` requantizer now; see the available input routes and prefer going back to original weights or a compatible import source

title: The download broke — must I restart it?
body: Current downloads support resume and verified-cache reuse, so it can be re-initiated; an interrupted build does not mean conversion can always resume in place — keep the diagnostics

title: How are MoE (mixture of experts) and Dense architectures identified automatically?
body: During inspection the backend decides MoE (mixture of experts, multi-expert FFN) or Dense from the config's architectures and expert fields (num_experts, num_local_experts, moe_intermediate_size); when it cannot decide it shows unknown. The result is used only to rank and label quantization/acceleration plans and show the processing route — it does not by itself change the artifact binary; available recipes are still decided by architecture, geometry, and input format, and being identified as MoE does not mean any MoE inference engine is wired

title: After a MoE model is produced, which inference engine is recommended dynamically by GPU model?
body: When identified as MoE, the backend gives a community inference-engine recommendation under the double condition "local GPU (compute_cap from nvidia-smi) + model on the engine's published list": only NVIDIA Blackwell (compute≥12.0, RTX 50 series, sm_120) AND a Basalt-published MoE (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) recommends Basalt (optimized for that architecture, native NVFP4, officially faster on Blackwell); MoE not on Basalt's adapted list such as Qwen3.6-35B-A3B defaults to Strata even on Blackwell, but a prominent compatibility note (compat_check, card turns warning-colored) is placed at the very top of the recommendation card: "Basalt is faster on this card, but this model is not on Basalt's adapted list (only Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Qwen3.8-27B). Verify yourself whether you can obtain or convert a compatible .basalt source before deciding to switch to the faster Basalt; if not, use the default engine below" — handing the "is the faster Basalt compatible" decision to the user instead of quietly sidestepping it; if that MoE is also not on Strata's published list, the note appends "defer to both engines' official repositories". Other NVIDIA (40/30/20 series), AMD, Intel, Apple, or no NVIDIA detected recommends Strata (broad support; Basalt only runs on Blackwell), with no compatibility note then (Basalt simply cannot run); a MoE architecture on neither published list gets Strata plus a "defer to the official repositories" note. The recommendation includes reason, hardware requirements, input format, supported models, alternatives, and official links, shown above the quantization plans. This is only a selection-advice display layer: it does not integrate engines, change the .ninfer artifact, or change engine download gates; Dense and unknown get no such recommendation. Differences in C12, hardware/format in C13/C14, resource boundaries in D11, format relations in J11, plain-language run steps in J12 (Basalt)/J13 (Strata)/J14 (Dense ninfer+kvmem)

title: What is quantization — does it change the model?
body: Representing weights with less information can reduce storage and may affect output; the source directory is not overwritten, and the output is a new artifact

title: How should I understand 2/3/4/5/6/8-bit?
body: An encoding-granularity metric, not a whole-model quality ranking; mixed plans and extra metadata make the actual bpw different

title: I picked 4-bit — why is the size not a quarter of the original?
body: Original dtype, mixed precision, scales, embeddings, heads, alignment, etc. affect size; reason from the real artifact, not the nominal bit width

title: Is 4-bit always faster than 8-bit?
body: Not necessarily; it depends on kernel, GPU, batch, context, bandwidth, and decode overhead; compare measurements under identical conditions

title: Is AWQ the same as ordinary Q4?
body: No; algorithm, calibration, packing, and runtime kernel differ; this project takes the isolated HF route

title: Which is better, GPTQ or AWQ?
body: There is no project-wide uniform conclusion; compare currently supported bit widths, task data, quality, and runtime cost — never fabricate a uniform ranking

title: Are MXFP4, NVFP4, and INT4 interchangeable?
body: Not just because they are 4-bit; floating-point encoding, scale, and layout contracts differ — use the exact recipe

title: Are Bonsai and GPTQ 2-bit the same thing?
body: No; ternary-source import and GPTQ calibrated encoding differ; available models, formats, and quality evidence are each independent

title: Is GGUF a quantization method?
body: It is a container/format system that can hold different tensor encodings; "GGUF" does not state a specific bit width or algorithm

title: Can restoring low bits to high bits recover ability?
body: Raising storage precision does not recover lost information; a second quantization may lose more — prefer the original full-precision source

title: Why are plans ranked by GPU generation, with NVFP4 recommended on RTX 50?
body: During inspection nvidia-smi reads compute_cap to identify the GPU generation: Blackwell (≥10.0, RTX 50 series) natively supports FP4/NVFP4, Ada/Hopper (≥8.9, RTX 40 series) natively supports FP8, Ampere (RTX 30 series) has no native FP8/FP4. The quantization plan list puts plans natively supported by this card first, then sorts by bpw, and uses gpu_note to say "native FP4 acceleration on this card" or "no native FP4 on this card; dequantization needed, not necessarily faster". Ranking and labeling are display advice only — they do not change the artifact or engine download gates, and do not replace the backend's "auto recommendation"; without GPU info it falls back to bpw sorting with no generation label. Native support is only a hardware capability; actual gains depend on measurements under identical conditions

title: What is the difference between Strata and Basalt, and which GPUs/scenarios does each suit?
body: Both are MIT-licensed open-source local MoE inference engines; Basalt is a fork of Strata. Strata (Niko1221/Strata) supports NVIDIA RTX 20/30/40/50, AMD, Intel Arc (Linux), Apple Silicon, takes standard GGUF, tiers experts GPU→RAM→SSD, has a one-click desktop app installer, and suits non-Blackwell/cross-platform/low-VRAM-large-RAM. Basalt (jesdga95/basalt) is NVIDIA Blackwell only (sm_120, compute 12.0) + CUDA 13 + driver R580+, takes self-contained .basalt v2, native NVFP4, officially fastest on Blackwell; its release package contains no CUDA/Python so you provide them, and it suits RTX 50 users chasing maximum speed. Both are OpenAI/Anthropic API compatible. Recommend by GPU + model: Blackwell AND model on Basalt's adapted list (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) → Basalt (faster); Blackwell but model not adapted (e.g. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) → default Strata, with a prominent compatibility note at the top of the card: "Basalt is faster but not adapted; verify compatibility yourself before deciding to switch"; other GPUs → Strata (Basalt cannot run). Speed numbers are for specific models/settings only and are not generalized into a universal guarantee

title: Does Basalt only support Blackwell GPUs, and what are the hardware/format requirements?
body: Yes. Basalt hard-requires an NVIDIA Blackwell GPU (compute capability 12.0 / sm_120) + CUDA 13; the system must be Linux x64 (AVX2, GCC13+, CMake3.24+) or Windows 10 1903+ x64 (MSVC/VS2022, Ninja), driver R580 branch or newer (Linux minimum 580.95.05). Non-Blackwell (40/30/20 series, AMD, Intel, Apple) cannot run it — use Strata instead. The release package (basalt-vX.Y.Z-windows-x64.zip / linux-x64.tar.gz) contains no CUDA libraries or Python environment; you must provide the CUDA 13 runtime (cudart, cuBLAS) on PATH and a Python 3.10+ .venv. Input is self-contained .basalt v2 (weights/tokenizer/MTP/vision projection/int8 tables); expert formats are Unsloth UD quants, Q8_0, NVFP4. Supports Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Qwen3.8-27B (dense, added in v0.4.0); does NOT include Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (that MoE is published by Strata only, so Blackwell defaults to Strata with a "Basalt is faster but not adapted; verify compatibility yourself" note at the top of the card). Experts that do not fit go to system RAM/SSD, with multi-GPU expert tiers. Start with bin/basalt serve --config basalt_config.json, default 127.0.0.1:8080

title: Which GPUs, VRAM, and RAM tiers does Strata support?
body: Strata supports NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20/30/40/50 series, AMD Radeon RX 7700/7800/7900, RX 9060/9070, AI PRO R9700 (RX 6800/6900 experimental), Intel Arc (Linux), Apple Silicon M1+, AMD Ryzen AI Max Strix Halo, NVIDIA DGX Spark (Linux). A 12GB-class consumer card is enough (README measurements include RTX 5070 12GB, RTX 3060 12GB); NVIDIA needs CUDA 13/driver 580+. RAM by tier (numbers = combined weight RAM+VRAM, leave extra OS headroom, estimates): Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA-DASLab Q2_0 about 37.6GB (fastest), IQ2_XS 39.2GB, IQ3_XXS 47GB, IQ3_S 54.8GB (best quality); Coder-only encoding about 32GB RAM; Unsloth 4–8bit needs 72–136GB. Experts tier GPU→RAM→SSD, takes standard GGUF; the provider recommends ISTA-DASLab→Unsloth→Gyro, with the user's explicit choice first. strata launch --plan only previews without downloading; one-click install via the desktop app or install.ps1/sh, OpenAI/Anthropic API. Supports Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, DeepSeekV4.1-Flash

title: Is the auto recommendation optimal?
body: It is a usable default under the wired rules, not a guarantee of best quality/speed; explain this run's actual auto-selection diagnostic

title: Why is the bit width I want missing?
body: Limited by architecture/geometry/input/format/engine; only available recipes are shown; the AI must not create an unimplemented route

title: Can 12GB VRAM run a 27B?
body: It depends on the specific model/bits, context, KV, speculative components, and free VRAM; historical Bonsai results do not guarantee every 27B

title: Are conversion RAM and inference VRAM the same?
body: Different stages/resources; explain the basis of the planner's current estimate — an unknown conversion peak is never filled with a number

title: Why does disk need to be larger than the final file?
body: Original download, extraction, intermediate processing weights, temporary output, and the final file occupy space at the same time

title: What if memory is not enough?
body: First see whether it is RAM/VRAM/disk; close occupying programs, switch to a suitable smaller model/recipe, adjust context/concurrency; lowering bits does not guarantee solving conversion-stage RAM

title: Can offloading to CPU guarantee it runs?
body: Look at the specific engine's current capabilities and parameters; a resource warning must not be explained as the project already providing arbitrary offload automatically

title: Why can the output location not be reused?
body: To prevent overwriting the original or existing artifacts; create a new separate empty output directory — never "solve" it by deleting the original model

title: I want quality first — how should I choose?
body: Start from the currently available higher-fidelity plans and a same-corpus baseline, and test your own task; do not treat bit width as the only criterion

title: Do parameter changes require re-conversion?
body: Distinguish weight quantization/processing parameters from runtime parameters; weight changes need a redo, serving parameters usually do not change weights, but explain the current generation-script/plan binding per the actual flow

title: What are the VRAM/RAM boundaries of the MoE engine recommendation — is a 12GB Blackwell enough?
body: Recommending by GPU only solves "which engine to pick", not "can it run/run fast". MoE expert weights mostly live in system RAM/SSD, with VRAM holding hot experts + attention; the threshold is the combination of VRAM + RAM + disk, not VRAM alone. Local example RTX 5070 Ti Laptop (Blackwell, 12GB) + about 31GB RAM: hits Basalt (driver≥R580), but under 12GB VRAM large MoE experts mostly land in RAM/SSD; Strata Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q2_0 needs about 37.6GB (RAM+VRAM), Coder about 32GB — this machine's RAM is tight, so pick a lower tier/leave enough headroom, with no guarantee of smoothly running the full 125B. Basalt likewise needs enough RAM for experts that do not fit in VRAM. First pick a pack by the engine's RAM tier table, use --plan/preview to see the resource plan, and measured speed is valid only for that specific setup. When resources are insufficient, switch to a smaller model/lower tier/add RAM — never speculate a guarantee

title: How do I choose among no abliteration, Abliteration, and Heretic?
body: Default none keeps the input; Abliteration does refusal-direction processing; Heretic needs an interactive save; none guarantees quality on every task

title: Why can GGUF/NVFP4 not be abliterated again?
body: Current import uses the quantized source directly; editing the HF base does not change imported tensors; to process, start from full precision first

title: Does an existing Heretic model need processing again?
body: Choose none when there is no need, to avoid stacked changes; the name alone cannot prove the processing method or quality

title: What is a direction file?
body: A refusal-direction vector matching the model's hidden size; validated against the specific supported format/source — never casually use another model's vector

title: Why does Heretic pop up a separate window?
body: The existing tool needs interaction and an artifact save; without saving complete weights in that window it will not continue pretending to be done

title: Is the calibration corpus for chatting?
body: It is used to estimate statistics for quantization/processing, not to automatically train arbitrary new knowledge; corpora at different stages serve different purposes

title: Can AWQ/GPTQ run without a corpus?
body: It can currently auto-prepare WikiText-2 train at a pinned revision; this needs network and resources, records sampling/hashes, and may not be the best fit for a domain task

title: Are more calibration samples always better?
body: Data representativeness, length, and count affect time and statistics; no monotonic improvement is promised — verify per task

title: What are group size, batch, and CPU activations?
body: Explain quantization grouping/processing batch and memory trade-offs; current HF group choice follows metadata, and CPU/disk offload adds time and RAM/disk pressure

title: Are imatrix, Engram, n-gram, and MTP sources the same?
body: No; they are respectively an importance matrix, an architecture-specific table, or speculative components — fill them per the current missing-source fields, never substituting one for another

title: What is speculative decoding?
body: An acceleration mechanism where a draft proposes tokens and the main model verifies them; it needs compatible components and implementation, and does not add ability to a model out of thin air

title: My model has no head — can it train one automatically?
body: Not currently; you can provide a supported external component, or choose auto/off — it cannot be force-enabled

title: After quantization/format conversion can MTP still be used, and why is it kept but not faster?
body: A compatible route keeps existing heads; kept does not mean enabled/faster; HF currently only archives, and execution needs a compatible NInfer. Look at runtime, the actual engine, acceptance, and a same-condition baseline

title: Can HF AWQ/GPTQ use MTP?
body: The current HF service does not execute it; auto with heads is blocked — to execute, use a compatible NInfer; when explicitly turned off it can archive only

title: Can MTP and DFlash2 be swapped freely?
body: No; architecture, geometry, weights, and config contracts differ; use only detected/compatible components

title: Are more draft tokens always faster?
body: Not guaranteed; more drafts add cost, and the gain depends on acceptance and hardware; test under identical conditions with available parameters

title: What is context, and why is there a 1024 cap?
body: Input and generation are bounded by the token window/current adapted engine; that small-model path has a specific cap, not a site-wide uniform cap for all models

title: Is KV cache bit width the same as weight quantization?
body: Different objects; the runtime cache affects VRAM and numerics; changing KV settings does not mean the main weights are requantized

title: What does high concurrency affect?
body: It increases simultaneous requests and resource overhead; the HF local service currently has generation concurrency 1 — do not assume it scaled just from a UI number

title: Will stopping the model and re-converting lose files?
body: What stops is the service process; normal artifacts are kept; the current page requires releasing the owned model service before converting, and the AI must not stop it on its own

title: It keeps saying "preparing" — is it stuck?
body: Look at the current download/install log, file growth, and errors — do not judge by time; the first run may be a large download, and no fixed progress is promised

title: If validation fails, does conversion still count as successful?
body: There may be a file but GPU use did not pass; runnability cannot be inferred from file existence; check the smoke-stage error

title: Difference between converted and validated?
body: converted only means converted (validation may have been skipped); validated has the corresponding validation evidence; direct start requires this run's verified state

title: Will refreshing the page lose the task?
body: Existing task state is recoverable; a backend restart/process interruption does not mean background execution continues — check the actual task record

title: Can I convert several at once, or convert while running?
body: The current BuildManager limits concurrent builds/service conflicts; wait per the UI hint or manually stop the owned service

title: Why does it say Torch CUDA is unavailable?
body: Confirm the actual worker's Torch and driver; having a GPU in the system does not mean that Python can use CUDA; prefer the one-click diagnostic log

title: Can the version-mismatch warning be ignored?
body: Distinguish warning/error; a version difference means insufficient compatibility evidence — a matching bundle/pinned engine reproduces more easily

title: After an interrupted build, which step resumes?
body: Current downloads are reusable, but an arbitrary conversion resume point is not guaranteed; keep logs, rebuild to a new output per task state, and never tamper with the manifest

title: The error shows only one line — what do I do?
body: Expand the current stage log and copy the redacted error with context; do not submit whole-drive paths, tokens, or complete model weights

title: The AI says it can continue, but the button is still disabled?
body: The backend gate decides; the AI can only explain — list the disable reason and locate it, and never let the user edit the state file to bypass

title: The model lost quality after quantization and got dumber — what now, and what is PPL?
body: Low bit width and unsuitable calibration corpus can increase quality loss; first look at the same-corpus PPL gate and real task performance, and if needed raise the bit width and use domain-matched independent calibration and evaluation sets. PPL is predictive perplexity on a given corpus, not accuracy on every task

title: How is the PPL increase computed?
body: `(current PPL / baseline PPL - 1) × 100%`; only a valid same-condition baseline makes it meaningful

title: Must the baseline model be exactly identical?
body: Source, tokenizer, processing stage, corpus, and evaluation settings should match; the pre/post-abliteration difference must not be treated as pure quantization loss

title: Is the 10% gate an official safe value?
body: It is a user-set acceptance threshold, not a universal quality guarantee; validate against your own application

title: Why can quality-rejected not start?
body: The currently chosen quality requirement was not met or measurement failed, and the system keeps the real report; adjust the plan/corpus and re-evaluate — editing the manifest directly is not advised

title: Does no PPL number mean zero loss?
body: No; look at not_measured/refused/measurement error — unknown is not 0

title: Why does the HF reference run on CPU?
body: The current full-precision reference path uses CPU FP32 while the quantized model uses GPU; it costs RAM/time, and dtype/device differences are also a comparison limitation

title: Can a packed model use itself as the baseline?
body: It cannot serve as a known full-precision baseline proving quantization lossless; without a confirmable reference the corresponding quality proof is refused

title: Can the calibration corpus also be the evaluation set?
body: Overlap should be avoided, following the current implementation's data isolation and traceability settings; otherwise results may be too optimistic

title: PPL passed but chat got worse — what now?
body: Add real-task tests for code/math/long context/instruction following; PPL does not cover every dimension, and checking the template and parameters is also necessary

title: Difference between prefill and decode?
body: The former processes the input prompt, the latter outputs token by token; the two tok/s numbers are not compared interchangeably

title: First token is slow but later ones fast — normal?
body: First load, input length, and prefill affect the first token; only measurement records can separate the specific bottleneck

title: measured/configured/refused/not_measured?
body: Respectively real measurement, configuration only, refused, and not measured; a configured number must not be advertised as measured performance

title: Why is my speed worse than the README?
body: GPU, model/revision, quantization, KV, context, speculation, concurrency, and test method differ; establish a same-condition baseline first

title: A 27B can do 180 tok/s — can I?
body: That is a specific historical RTX 5070 Ti Laptop+Bonsai+MTP3 measurement and cannot be extrapolated; cite it with source/conditions

title: Does a high acceptance rate mean MTP is good?
body: Corpus and method affect results; acceptance on a historical tiled corpus does not represent real requests

title: Is the Torch peak the GPU's total usage?
body: No; the current HF metric basis is Torch's allocation peak, excluding all process/driver overhead or the quantization-stage total peak

title: It was estimated to fit — why actual OOM?
body: Beyond weights there are KV, activations, temporary buffers, other applications, and stage differences; estimates have assumptions — diagnose by the actual stage

title: Can two reports of the same quantization be compared directly?
body: Hardware, input, context, KV, concurrency, and speculation must also align; different sampling settings are not evidence of algorithm superiority

title: How do I verify faster without obviously worse?
body: Fix input/runtime config for a speed baseline, then look at same-corpus quality and real tasks; show measurement conditions and limitations with the results

title: After conversion, how do I actually run it?
body: Confirm this run is validated/gate passed → click Start model API → wait for ready → copy the returned base_url → fill the model ID in the client → verify with a short sentence

title: What opens a `.ninfer`?
body: A matching NInfer engine/the page-generated launch script; not every GGUF/HF loader recognizes it

title: Where is the AWQ/GPTQ artifact and how do I run it?
body: Current output is `model-hf/`, via the isolated HF worker; after validation, start from the page or the generated `scripts/run.bat` — do not load with NInfer

title: Why does it say the port is occupied?
body: Stop the occupying service you clearly own, or change the port per the current flow and update/rebuild the plan; never let the AI kill unknown processes

title: starting never changes?
body: A process starting is not ready; look at the current serve.log, model loading, VRAM, port, and exit state

title: What goes in base_url in the client?
body: Copy the actual service-returned `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1`; if the client wants a full endpoint, append `/chat/completions` once

title: How do I fill the model name?
body: Read the real id from that service's `/v1/models`; not a guess from the file name or UI label; when a service does not support listing, fill it manually per config

title: Does the local API need a key?
body: The current built-in HF loopback service has no such auth requirement; when a client forces one, use its required placeholder value, but that is not authentication; other engines/upstreams follow their actual service config

title: Can it connect to chat software, images, or tool calls?
body: Text-compatible clients can integrate per the interface; the current HF does not support images, tools, structured output, or arbitrary parameters — text compatibility does not promise every feature

title: Can another computer access it?
body: Default loopback is local-only; public deployment needs added authentication/permissions/network protection — simply changing host does not make it safely done

title: Can the produced .ninfer run directly in Strata or Basalt, and which should I use after conversion?
body: No. .ninfer is only for the matching NInfer; Strata needs a separate GGUF download and Basalt a separate .basalt — neither can be fed .ninfer directly. The page's "Inference engine recommendation" gives one by architecture and GPU, with repository links. Dense uses ninfer-fusion-kvmem (J14, https://github.com/1314521gjy/ninfer-fusion-kvmem, Apache-2.0; melis2023/ninfer-kvmem-actkv has no LICENSE and is not recommended). MoE with compute exactly 12.0 AND model Flash-Next or DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash uses Basalt (J12, https://github.com/jesdga95/basalt). Other MoE uses Strata (J13, https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata); datacenter compute 10.0 is not RTX 50. These recommendations do not integrate or auto-download.

title: Complete plain-language steps to run MoE with Basalt on an RTX 50 card?
body: Applies to: compute exactly 12.0, Win10 1903+ or Win11, model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next or DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. compute 10.0 and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B go to J13. Never treat .ninfer as .basalt. ① Provide CUDA 13, driver R580+, Python 3.10+ yourself; open https://github.com/jesdga95/basalt/releases and download basalt-v0.4.0-windows-x64.zip. ② Separately download the matching .basalt v2. ③ First ask separately for context tokens and concurrency; do not write the script before getting positive integers. ④ basalt_config.json contains only the verified structure: version=2, models[0].model=the user's absolute .basalt path, gpu="0", kv per model default (Flash-Next fp16, DeepSeek fp8), server.port=8080. Writing an unverified concurrency field is forbidden; when concurrency > 1 the bat first echoes "This run starts with a single request". ⑤ start-basalt.bat uses cmd only: @echo off, chcp 65001, setlocal EnableExtensions, cd /d "%~dp0"; if the engine or model is missing then echo, pause, exit /b 1. Launch line: "bin\\basalt.exe" serve --config "%~dp0basalt_config.json" --max-context user-context. End with pause. ⑥ Open http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/models then send a short chat.

title: Complete plain-language steps to run MoE with Strata on a non-RTX-50 card (or Qwen3.6-35B-A3B)?
body: Applies to: MoE with compute not 12.0, and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on any card. Never rename .ninfer to GGUF. ① Open https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/releases and install Strata-0.2.13-windows-x64-setup.exe; confirm strata.exe works. ② Separately download GGUF: 35B-A3B uses Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL, UD-Q6_K_XL or Q8_0; Flash-Next uses ISTA-DASLab Q2_0, IQ2_XS, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S. ③ First ask separately for context tokens and concurrency. The only verified command is strata launch --family --model --plan; no context or concurrency flag has been verified. ④ start-strata.bat uses cmd only: @echo off, chcp 65001, setlocal EnableExtensions, cd /d "%~dp0"; if where strata.exe fails or the GGUF does not exist then echo, pause, exit /b 1. Before launching, echo the user's requested context and concurrency and state "the currently verified command cannot pass these two". The preview command writes only strata.exe launch --family user-family --model user-tier --plan. After user confirmation a second bat drops --plan. Adding unverified flags is forbidden. End with pause. ⑤ Use the address printed by the process to open /v1/models then send a short chat. NVIDIA needs CUDA 13, driver 580+.

title: Complete plain-language steps to run a Dense model with ninfer+kvmem?
body: Applies to: Dense .ninfer produced by TurboForge. Recommended: https://github.com/1314521gjy/ninfer-fusion-kvmem (Apache-2.0). https://github.com/melis2023/ninfer-kvmem-actkv has no LICENSE and is not recommended. ① Use only Releases tag engine-v0.11.0-kvmem-20261008. On RTX 50 use ninfer-serve-120a.exe, 40 series -89, 30 series -86, and verify SHA256SUMS.txt. Put engine and model on an English path. ② The assistant must first ask separately for context token count and concurrency count; do not write the script before getting positive integers. ③ Write start-fusion.bat, cmd only: @echo off, chcp 65001, setlocal EnableExtensions, cd /d "%~dp0"; if not exist engine or model then echo, pause, exit /b 1. In the same bat set NINFER_KV_WINDOW=16384, NINFER_KV_RETRIEVE=8192, NINFER_HOST_PAGEABLE=1, NINFER_KV_REUSE_HOSTBACKED=1; for a ternary model also set NINFER_TERNARY_KVMEM_SCORE_QUERY_TAIL=64. The launch line writes the user's context into --max-context and the user's concurrency into --max-concurrency, with --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8091 --kv-dtype k8v4 --host-kv-mib 16384 --prefill-chunk 1024 --max-shared-prefixes 0. On a 12GB card use --kv-capacity 8192; only larger VRAM may use the documented 17920; --host-kv-mib 16384 needs at least 16GB free RAM — if not enough, ask the user first then reduce. Last line pause. ④ Do not add --spec yet. After the window shows engine ready, open another terminal to http://127.0.0.1:8091/v1/models, then ask "17+25, reply with the number only". When the request is longer than --kv-capacity the answer is untrustworthy — switch to the repository's gateway\\chat_gateway.py. ⑤ Troubleshooting: missing DLL → put CUDA 13/FFmpeg/libcurl beside the exe; insufficient VRAM → lower --kv-capacity first; CUDA Graph failure → add --no-cuda-graph; a Chinese path that cannot be read → switch to an English path.

title: Where do the AI's URL, model, and key come from?
body: Provided by the user's chosen vendor/self-hosted service; fill the actual compatible API root address, model ID, and access key; this project bundles no quota

title: Is the assistant the same as the model I want to convert?

title: Why does the connection test fail?
body: Check in order: address root path, model ID, auth/permissions, quota, network/certificates, and protocol capability; explain per the real error — never let the user paste the key into chat

title: Is a key in `.env` absolutely never leaked?
body: Plaintext config still needs backend isolation, ignore/packaging exclusion, file permissions, and log redaction; it must not go in VITE variables or the frontend bundle

title: Where is the key entered in the dialog saved?
body: The first-version design defaults to backend session memory, lost on restart/expiry; only after an admin enables it and the user explicitly chooses is it saved to the local `.env`

title: Why is the config different after refresh/restart?
body: Explain the actual source by the priority of session override, environment variables, `.env`; restart clears memory; environment variables may override the just-saved file

title: Which page content is sent to the cloud?
body: Selected text, the question, and the redacted business summary checked in the preview; logs are not attached by default and can be edited/deleted before sending; the target domain is shown clearly

title: Can I keep everything off the external network entirely?
body: Choose an explicitly allowed local compatible service or use offline help only; a third-party service's retention policy depends on that service — the project cannot guarantee it for them

title: Will the AI change config or run commands automatically?
body: The first version is read-only and navigation; answers do not execute; normal business operations still use the existing buttons and gates

title: What if the AI answers wrong, finds nothing, or runs out of quota?
body: Look at knowledge citations/actual diagnostics and use offline help; provide the redacted question and request ID; never treat an AI answer as proof of successful execution

title: Can I move the artifact to another machine and just run it?
body: It needs the same format support, matching engine/runtime/driver, and paths; generated scripts may contain the original path and need checking — cross-machine plug-and-play is not guaranteed

title: Which files can I delete to save space?
body: Distinguish original model, download cache, intermediate weights, final artifact, and dedicated environment; stop tasks/services and check dependencies first — never auto-delete in an answer

title: Will user data be packed into a shared bundle?
body: The release script should explicitly exclude models/cache/secrets/sessions; go by the actual ZIP inspection, not just `.gitignore`

title: The source updated — why does the AI still describe old features?
body: Check the running package version and knowledge version; business changes update entries and coverage tests in sync — never feed stale docs to the model as-is

title: How do I report a problem so maintainers understand?
body: Include version/route, redacted model identifier, stage/error code, relevant log excerpt, and request ID; no keys/weights/private full paths

title: Why did it succeed before and fail now?
body: Compare model revision/file hashes, tool versions, environment and resources, runtime parameters; do not attribute it to the quantization algorithm without evidence

title: Where are historical reports, and can they be reproduced?
body: Look at the actual location of the current manifest/artifacts; reproduction needs the corresponding inputs/versions/commands — never graft numbers from another build

title: Can I ignore a warning?
body: Analyze that warning's specific risk and stage; a warning does not always block, but an error/quality rejection must not be skipped as an ordinary hint

title: My error is not in the help — what now?
body: Show the unknown error and stage, collect bounded redacted evidence; provide general path/permission/resource/service diagnostics — never guess a nonexistent code

title: Is there a mode that "guarantees zero difficulty for every model"?
body: Not currently; the dynamic support matrix, specific errors, and in-app help lower the operation barrier, but external permission/hardware/algorithm limits cannot be removed

For a complete HF fill only this field; for GGUF pick the specific file; a path existing does not mean the format is supported; the path is not sent to the external assistant

title: Original model source; Original HF directory
body: Supplies the matching config, tokenizer, or full-precision tensors required by the route for an already-quantized source. Default/constraints: Shown by default; leave empty for a complete HF model; required when the source is missing. The supported self-contained Qwen3.5-0.8B Q8_0 GGUF generates config/tokenizer/template automatically and needs no source; a traditional GGUF source directory needs config.json and tokenizer.json/tokenizer.model, and a directory containing only GGUF cannot be selected; explicit repository links are supported; the source is never guessed from the file name and never depends on the developer's local directory

title: Repository GGUF file
body: Pick the specific file and shards in a multi-precision repository; the input precision follows the file. Default/constraints: The user chooses explicitly; precision is never guessed

title: Output directory
body: Stores new artifacts, plans, logs, and reports; intermediate files may take more space. Default/constraints: Assigned automatically or chosen by the user as a new empty directory outside the original model; source weights are never overwritten

title: Target bit width; Quantization plan; Quantization target
body: Choose the quantization target directly: plan options state the bit width, algorithm, and engine; the bit-width dropdown only filters by main-weight precision; there is no longer a "usage preference" that silently picks a plan for the user. Default/constraints: Candidates = verified recipes for the current model + engine; unadapted bit widths are not listed, so the menu may be short; auto recommendation is a usable default following the model's default policy, not a guarantee of optimality; lower bits do not guarantee more speed or unchanged quality

title: Published ternary GGUF
body: A ready-made PQ2_0 source matching Bonsai 2; no new ternary model is trained. Default/constraints: Optional; required when that recipe is enabled; architecture/geometry must match

title: Conversion device
body: Controls whether conversion computes on CUDA or a supported CPU route; it does not change the inference engine. Default/constraints: From meta.defaults.device; CPU routes have no uniform speed measurement

title: Allow approximate requantization
body: Expresses the user's explicit consent to the loss of approximately decoding and requantizing already-quantized weights; lost information is not restored. Default/constraints: Off by default; it cannot lift real limits such as unadapted formats/architectures

title: Abliteration method
body: none keeps existing weight behavior; Abliteration/Heretic rewrites supported full-precision weights and may affect task quality. Default/constraints: Default none; imported quantized weights cannot be processed again; Heretic needs an interactive save

title: Calibration corpus
body: UTF-8 text used by AWQ/GPTQ to estimate quantization statistics; representativeness affects results and time. Default/constraints: Leave empty to prepare WikiText-2 train at the current pinned revision; never mixed with evaluation data

title: Group size
body: One group of weights shares quantization parameters, affecting metadata overhead, statistics, and compatibility. Default/constraints: Current new-calibration default 128, options 32/64/128; existing packed layouts follow their own contract

title: Calibration samples
body: Number of calibration samples; more may increase time, memory, and data coverage, but quality is not guaranteed to improve monotonically. Default/constraints: Current HF default 128; the allowed range is validated by the backend

title: Tokens per sample
body: Length of each calibration sample; affects activation scale and usable corpus. Default/constraints: Current HF default 512; cannot exceed the model's actual window; short samples never silently switch the algorithm

title: HF inference backend
body: torch uses compatible compute; auto lets GPTQModel choose, and some optimized kernels need extra build tools. Default/constraints: Default torch; HF runs in an isolated environment; quantized packed weights are not handed to NInfer

title: Speculative decoding
body: Uses compatible existing MTP/DFlash2 components; when disabled, heads that should be kept are still kept. Default/constraints: Default auto; an explicit request without the component is refused. HF does not run heads; auto with heads blocks the route

title: Serving context
body: The token window used by input, generation, and cache; larger values raise VRAM pressure. Default/constraints: The effective value comes from the runtime profile; geometry/engine caps cannot be broken by typing a bigger number

title: Max concurrency
body: Number of simultaneous requests; affects cache/compute resources and throughput. Default/constraints: Takes the meta/runtime default; HF generation currently requires 1

title: Serving port
body: The listen port of the local model API on this PC; different from the page/external assistant service address. Default/constraints: Default takes the port of the first origin in TURBOFORGE_AI_ALLOWED_LOCAL_ORIGINS in .env (template 18080); 1–65535 and not in use; changes take effect through the existing plan/script flow

title: Post-conversion smoke test
body: A real GPU load plus a short generation provides runnable evidence; it does not replace a full quality evaluation. Default/constraints: Enabled by default; HF cannot skip it. converted must not be treated as validated

title: Benchmark speed; Post-conversion speed benchmark (quality evaluation optional)
body: Runs the real speed/optional PPL test supported by the current route, adding time; when off, unmeasured means unknown. Default/constraints: From the current user choice/guided-mode default; the gate depends on the corresponding evaluation

title: Benchmark repetitions
body: Repeated tests help observe variance and also add time. Default/constraints: Current default and range come from benchmark/profile; HF has a repetition limit and never reruns infinitely by default

title: Benchmark KV precision
body: Affects only the test cache/runtime numerics and VRAM; it does not change the main-weight encoding. Default/constraints: Follows geometry automatically; bf16/rk4v4 speed and quality must be verified on the corresponding engine

title: Evaluation corpus; Perplexity text
body: Scores on the given UTF-8 text; new HF quantization may leave it empty to use the pinned test set automatically, up to 2048 tokens. Default/constraints: Kept separate from calibration train; NInfer needs a manual corpus and baseline; full paths are excluded by default

title: Perplexity corpus manifest
body: Uses a supported scored-corpus description instead of ordinary free text. Default/constraints: Chosen against Perplexity text under the existing contract; must be valid and version-consistent

title: Baseline model; Baseline artifact
body: A baseline with the same source/tokenizer/processing stage is used to measure the difference. Default/constraints: NInfer users provide a verified baseline; HF currently uses this run's post-processing full-precision CPU FP32 reference; packed weights cannot prove themselves lossless

title: Quality gate
body: Requires the PPL comparison to pass before a direct start; a failed measurement must not be disguised as a pass. Default/constraints: On by default for guided-mode new HF quantization and can be explicitly turned off; NInfer follows the user choice; it cannot replace code/math/long-text evaluation

title: Allowed PPL increase
body: The user's acceptance threshold for the relative increase `(current/baseline - 1)×100%`; not an official safety guarantee. Default/constraints: The page's common initial value is 10%, decided by the user's task requirements; editing the manifest to bypass a failure is not allowed

title: Prefill length list
body: Benchmark input token lengths; affect prefill load and measurement comparability. Default/constraints: From profile/benchmark; comma-separated valid lengths, bounded by geometry caps

title: Generation length list
body: Benchmark output token counts; affect decode time and the test basis. Default/constraints: Takes the current profile/user values; HF does not support arbitrary numbers of generation lengths

title: Perplexity context
body: The PPL scoring window length; not the quantization bit width or training length. Default/constraints: Bounded by the model's actual window; the baseline must use the same effective value

title: Perplexity stride
body: The scoring sliding-window step; affects overlap and the number of scores. Default/constraints: Greater than 0 and less than the actual PPL context; baseline conditions match, and repeated counting must not pose as new corpus

title: Benchmark corpus ids
body: A token-ID corpus used by a specific tool to generate a reproducible load. Default/constraints: Uses the current compatible format; acceptance on a tiled corpus does not represent real user requests

title: NInfer converter source directory
body: Matched source containing tools/convert; the origin of the converter program. Default/constraints: Prepared automatically or chosen by the user at a pinned revision; a different revision needs a compatibility check

title: NInfer engine directory
body: Contains ninfer.exe/ninfer-serve.exe and DLLs; affects actual load/generation support. Default/constraints: Prepared automatically or chosen as a matching bundle; conversion support does not mean the engine supports running

title: idle / created / starting / planned
body: Waiting, starting, or planned; the artifact is not yet proven runnable — see the next stage. Launch: No

title: preparing
body: Downloading/installing and preparing files; see the current preparation log. Launch: No

title: jailbreaking / jailbroken / converting
body: Weight processing or conversion in progress; finished processing is not finished GPU validation. Launch: No

title: converted
body: The artifact was generated; this run has not completed the corresponding GPU validation. Launch: No

title: validating / benchmarking
body: Validating or measuring; wait for real results — progress is not a score. Launch: No

title: validated
body: This build passed validation; backend conditions such as task completion, the quality gate, and artifact/component checks still apply. Launch: Subject to the actual backend start gate

title: blocked / failed / crashed / interrupted
body: Blocked by planning, build failed, or interrupted; see the specific diagnostic/stage — editing the state file to bypass is not allowed. Launch: No

title: validation-failed
body: GPU load/generation validation failed; check the actual smoke log. Launch: No

title: quality-rejected
body: The current quality requirement failed or evaluation failed; check the source, corpus, baseline, and actual metrics. Launch: No

title: server: starting
body: The process is loading; the health check has not passed yet — see serve.log. Launch: Wait for ready

title: server: ready
body: The local model health check passed; the next step is still one real text request. Launch: Running; not a guarantee of task quality

title: server: stopped / exited
body: Not running or the process exited; confirm the current build validation and service errors. Launch: Not running

title: Refusal direction vector
body: Precomputed refusal direction (.npy / .pt, length equal to hidden_size, exportable from heretic). Required when transformers is not installed; otherwise leave empty to collect it automatically from calibration prompts.. Parameter type: path; the default comes from current metadata/processor results — missing values are never guessed.

title: Calibration layer index
body: Hidden-layer index for collecting activations; empty uses num_hidden_layers // 2.. Parameter type: int; the default comes from current metadata/processor results — missing values are never guessed.

title: Harmful calibration prompts
body: One per line; empty uses the built-in default set. Only used when calibration is needed.. Parameter type: string_list; the default comes from current metadata/processor results — missing values are never guessed.

title: Harmless calibration prompts
body: One per line; empty uses the built-in default set. Only used when calibration is needed.. Parameter type: string_list; the default comes from current metadata/processor results — missing values are never guessed.

title: Output projection suffixes
body: Output tensor suffixes to orthogonalize; empty uses the default set. Advanced option.. Parameter type: string_list; the default comes from current metadata/processor results — missing values are never guessed.

title: Embedding tensor suffixes
body: Embedding tensor suffixes to process; empty uses the default set. Advanced option.. Parameter type: string_list; the default comes from current metadata/processor results — missing values are never guessed.

title: NVFP4 quantized checkpoint
body: An existing NVFP4 checkpoint; it must match the producer layout. Not provided by default; supply only when the current recipe/feature needs it. The actual source and shapes must pass backend validation.

title: GGUF weights
body: The complete file and shards of an already-quantized GGUF. Not provided by default; supply only when the current recipe/feature needs it. The actual source and shapes must pass backend validation.

title: PQ2_0 ternary GGUF
body: A published PQ2_0 ternary source with matching geometry; no new weights are trained. Not provided by default; supply only when the current recipe/feature needs it. The actual source and shapes must pass backend validation.

title: Importance matrix (imatrix)
body: An importance matrix matching the current model tensors. Not provided by default; supply only when the current recipe/feature needs it. The actual source and shapes must pass backend validation.

title: Engram table GGUF
body: The Engram table required by the specified architecture. Not provided by default; supply only when the current recipe/feature needs it. The actual source and shapes must pass backend validation.

title: External MTP component
body: An external MTP component compatible with the current model; it is not retrained. Not provided by default; supply only when the current recipe/feature needs it. The actual source and shapes must pass backend validation.

title: External DFlash2 checkpoint
body: A DFlash2 checkpoint with an explicit compatibility declaration; it is not the same as plain DFlash. Not provided by default; supply only when the current recipe/feature needs it. The actual source and shapes must pass backend validation.

title: n-gram table
body: An n-gram table for a supported architecture; when absent, the real route is used. Not provided by default; supply only when the current recipe/feature needs it. The actual source and shapes must pass backend validation.
